core.title: Keep the cross-unit produce/consume graph acyclic
core.given: A plan's units (the composition units the profile names, each a bounded slice of the product) declare produce/consume entries by artifact NAME, forming a directed graph with an edge producer-unit -> consumer-unit whenever a name produced by one unit is consumed by another.
core.when: You author, edit or review any plan containing such units, whether or not your change touches produce/consume entries.
core.then: Ensure the name-keyed unit graph is acyclic: no strongly-connected component may contain more than one unit, including cycles that already existed.
prefer: Before adding an edge producer B -> consumer A (A consumes a name B produces), check by artifact name whether a path A -> B already exists; if it does, the new edge would close a cycle.
When a loop exists, restructure unit boundaries or artifact ownership so dependencies flow one way.
avoid: Reasoning about unit dependencies via the plan format's linkage field instead of the produce/consume artifact name, when the profile records that field as optional or nullable and therefore not a reliable key.
Mutual or transitive produce/consume loops between two or more units.
Hiding a loop by nulling or renaming the plan format's linkage field while the artifact names still loop.
core.why: A cross-unit produce/consume cycle means no unit in the loop can be delivered before the others; the graph must be a DAG so units can be ordered. Artifact names key the edges; whether the plan format's linkage field could serve as a key is a schema fact supplied by the profile, and an optional or nullable field is not a reliable key.
evidence: SCC analysis of the name-keyed unit graph (nodes = units, edges producer -> consumer by artifact name) reports no component with more than one unit.
verification: Generic check: nodes are the plan's units; add a directed edge producer-unit -> consumer-unit whenever an artifact NAME produced by one unit is consumed by another; run strongly-connected-component analysis and report every SCC containing more than one unit as a violation, whether pre-existing or newly introduced.

Edges are keyed on the produce/consume artifact name, never on the plan format's linkage field; that field's local name and schema properties (in particular its nullability) are supplied by the profile, and only the profile decides whether it could ever be a reliable key.
Change-level attribution (whether the current change produced the entry that closed the cycle) only labels findings; it is not a precondition for firing, so pre-existing cycles are still violations.

fires: A planner adds a consume entry to unit A for an artifact name produced by unit B, while A already (directly or transitively) feeds B by artifact name.
A planner splits a unit and the two resulting units each consume an artifact name the other produces.
Two units have null or absent linkage fields but share produce/consume artifact names forming a loop.
A planner makes an unrelated edit (e.g. only to a linkage field) in a plan whose unit graph already contains a multi-unit SCC: the existing cycle is still a violation.
doesNotFire: A unit produces and consumes artifact names only internally (an SCC of size one unit).
Cross-unit produce/consume edges exist but form a DAG (e.g. A->B->C with no path back).
The work involves no units or produce/consume entries at all.

profileRequirements.meaning: What the stack calls the plan's composition unit -- the bounded slice of the product that a plan decomposes work into and whose produce/consume artifact-name entries form the dependency graph; also the term matched in task/plan text for activation.

The plan artifact's optional cross-unit linkage/reference field (the core's 'plan format's linkage field'): its local field name and its schema properties -- in particular whether it is optional or nullable -- which determine whether it may serve as a key for dependency edges. The core never keys the produce/consume graph on this field and treats nulling or renaming it as a gaming move.
profileRequirements.bunValue: contract -- the plan artifact's linkage field, nullable corpus-wide

neutralityNotes: The rule is otherwise fully stack-neutral: it constrains only the plan's declared name-keyed produce/consume graph, with no code, path, suffix or tooling content. (1) 'wagon' is generalized to the plan's composition unit ('unit') and instantiated per stack through roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_unit (Bun: wagon); the vocabulary knows a wagon's directory (layout.wagon_dir) and URN shape (urn.wagon) but bun.json contains no path or URN value to bind those keys to. (2) 'contract field' is generalized to 'the plan format's linkage field'; its local name and schema properties (nullability) are plan-schema idiom values bound through idiom.plan_syntax#linkage_field (Bun: contract, nullable corpus-wide). The core makes every claim about that field conditional on the profile's schema facts -- it never asserts nullability unconditionally -- so instantiated with the Bun profile the obligation is exactly Bun's (the linkage field is nullable, hence artifact names are the only reliable key), while in a stack whose format has no such field, or a non-nullable one, the linkage-field clauses are vacuous or inapplicable and the name-keyed acyclicity obligation stands unchanged; the core is therefore neither weaker nor stronger. (3) The finding/term id consume_cycle and the detector reference are realization details kept in bunOnly; per-rule severity 3 and strict disposition are carried in core:verification, not the profile.
